ModMetaData.name: TailorMade Waistlines
ModMetaData.author: Nelim
ModMetaData.description:
Decides where garments stop on the body. An add-on to TailorMade, not affiliated with it.
TailorMade sorts apparel into classes and fits each class into a horizontal band of the body — pants into the bottom 58%, boots into the bottom 20%, chest pieces into the top 55%. Those numbers suit a body drawn with legs. On a body retexture drawn as one legless shape, 58% of the way up from the hem lands above the navel, and trousers read as a high-waisted skirt.
They are constants, and nothing exposes them. This mod makes them settings, so every leg garment of every mod is corrected at once. Nothing changes until a slider moves: the defaults are TailorMade's own values.
It also offers to lift one of TailorMade's own guards, carefully. TailorMade only bands a torso garment whose art already starts 40% of the way up the texture. That guard exists so long coats and capes keep draping to the ankles, and it is right to — but it also excludes the garments that most need shortening: a vanilla shirt is drawn over the whole body, so it stays full length and hides the trousers entirely. The option lifts the test for on-skin garments only. Shirts and tribalwear are shortened; dusters, parkas, jackets and robes are worn on the shell layer and still drape. The shirt is compressed into the band rather than cut off at it, so the option is off by default.
This mod gives no garment a texture. Vanilla trousers carry no worn graphic at all, so a mod that fills that field is still required — any of the visible-pants mods will do.
[b]Thanks[/b] to astryl, whose TailorMade does all the work this one merely aims, and whose MIT licence is what makes an add-on like this possible; to brrainz for Harmony; to aedbia, whose AB's Visible Pants supplies the trousers vanilla never draws; and to the author of WDI's Realistic Bodies, whose art is the reason the problem exists at all.
[b]Made with AI.[/b] The preview and the icon were generated by an image model and recomposed by hand. The assembly, its tests and its documentation were written with Claude Code, which the commit history records as a co-author.
[b]Adoption.[/b] If I do not answer within a reasonable time after being contacted, anyone may freely update this or any other of my mods, including publishing a continuation of it. All credit must be preserved.
